- Optional: reconcile the webhook-loss theory (check GitHub delivery logs) — if push events for machine merges are being dropped, the belt above is the durable fix regardless.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: no agents-side fix waits >15 min in main without a release cut (metric on the board or tick log line).
2. AC2: manual dispatch remains safe/idempotent (no double release for the same content — the version ledger dedupes).
3. AC3: docs/README paths still don't cut releases (paths-ignore preserved).
4. AC4: live — after ship, #841-class fixes activate without operator involvement.

## Test plan

- L1: rule unit tests (main-ahead detection with ignored-path diffs).
- L2: replay the 2026-10-10 14:24-17:05 timeline — the belt would have fired at ~14:39.
- L3 (live): next agents fix merges; release appears without human action.

## Non-goals

- Changing the pack format or compile steps.
- The release workflow's internal steps — only its TRIGGERING reliability.

## References

- Instance: #841 merged 14:24Z; no release until operator dispatch 17:05Z; #826 hung in the gap.
- Context: fa engine pin incident 2026-10-10 (factory_ref) — same "fix merged ≠ live" class."
  }
}

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

The ticket asks for a "belt" — the SM tick (or a kicker rule) compares latest release tag's commit vs main HEAD each tick; when main is ahead on non-ignored paths and no release run is pending → dispatch workflow_dispatch.

Wait — this is a bug development pack. The ticket is gh-844. Let me look at the repo structure to understand what exists. The instructions say write RCA, write a reproduction test that fails, then fix.

The task: The push trigger silently skipped merges. The durable fix: a kicker in the SM tick that detects main-ahead-on-non-ignored-paths and dispatches workflow_dispatch.

blocks.text:
# Agent pack release (dmtools-agents#441).
#
# Builds and publishes per-agent versioned packs — one self-contained zip per
# affected agent (<agent>-<version>.zip + manifest.json + .sha256) — so
# consumers fetch a single agent over plain HTTPS instead of a git submodule.
#
# The pack format is built by `dmtools compile` (dm.ai#595) — the runtime repo
# owns the single implementation; this workflow only orchestrates: test →
# compute affected set → bump versions.json → compile → validate → publish.
#
# Triggers:
#   push to main            — affected set from the diff since the last release tag
#   workflow_dispatch       — manual; `agents=all` or `agents=name1,name2`,
#                             `bump` selects patch/minor/major (default patch)
name: Agent Pack Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      # CI-only changes never cut a release. NOTE: '**.md' is deliberately
      # NOT ignored — agent instruction packs ship .md files (instructions/
      # joined the default agents in a57b3ba); ignoring them let runner
      # configs reference pack files the published zips never carried
      # (live: 2026-10-01 dev-leg failure, story_development-0.1.11).
      - '.github/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'site/**'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agents:
        description: "'all' or a comma-separated agent list (default: affected set)"
        required: false
        default: ''
      bump:
        description: 'Version bump'
        required: false
        default: 'patch'
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
      dry_run:
        description: 'Build + validate without publishing'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: agent-pack-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # publish the GitHub Release + commit versions.json

jobs:
  release:
    # The JS unit-test suite is NOT re-run here (owner 2026-10-01): quality.yml
    # runs it on every PR and main's protection is strict (required `crap` +
    # up-to-date), so every commit reaching main already passed the suite on a
    # current head. The release only computes the affected set, compiles,
    # validates and publishes.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history for the since-last-release diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' resolves to the current release tag (owner mandate 2026-10-01).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
            TAG="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "DMTOOLS_VERSION=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "::notice::dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${TAG}"
          fi

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        env:
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION || vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Compute base ref (last release tag, if any)
        id: base
        run: |
          last_tag=$(git tag --list 'agents-rel-*' --sort=-creatordate | head -1)
          echo "ref=${last_tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "base ref: ${last_tag:-<none — first release, all agents>}"

      - name: Sync to current main (queued runs release current main)
        # The concurrency group serializes release runs, but actions/checkout
        # gives each run its own TRIGGER SHA — a run queued behind another
        # computed its affected set and version bumps from a ledger that
        # pre-dated the previous run's ledger PR (live 2026-10-04, gh-690:
        # three content PRs merged within 3 min → overlapping releases
        # double-bumped sm_github/pr_review to 0.1.24 and cut the empty
        # ledger PR #689). Reset to origin/main so base-tag...HEAD covers
        # exactly the unreleased content ONCE, from the current ledger; a
        # queued run that finds everything already released writes
        # dist/.no-release and no-ops. Gated to push events — a manual
        # dispatch may deliberately target a non-main ref.
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        run: |
          git fetch origin main
          git reset --hard origin/main

      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
          # gh-812: the builder reads the previous release's shipped catalog
          # and same-version pack zips (version uniqueness + payload compare).
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # gh-812 rework (review thread 3): untrusted tag names reach the
          # script ONLY through env indirection — never template-expanded
          # into the run: block. Actions interpolates ${{ }} BEFORE bash
          # parses the script, so a crafted agents-rel-* tag name (any user
          # with push access can create one; the newest by creatordate wins)
          # could break out of the quoting and run arbitrary code in this
          # contents:write job.
          BASE_REF: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
          PREV_RELEASE_TAG: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-812 rework: release-base tags are machine-generated
          # (agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS); anything else in the newest

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:

  # pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists,
  # will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its

  # factory-data snapshots, dev waves) cancelled every other branch's

  # canonical pin is bumped (separate PR): until then the called
  # workflow's own global group still supersedes.

permissions:

jobs:

    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).

        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);

        run: |

            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# gh-844 — Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The agent-pack release (`agent-pack-release.yml` push trigger) silently
skipped two consecutive main merges on 2026-10-10 (14:24Z gh-841, ~16:00Z gh-843);
agents-side fixes sat unreleased in main for 2.75h until an operator's manual
`workflow_dispatch` (17:05Z), hanging #826 in the gap.

**Root cause**: The release pipeline has exactly ONE trigger plane — the GitHub
`push` event on main. When a push event is dropped server-side (webhook-loss
theory; delivery logs not reconciled), nothing anywhere detects that main is
ahead of the latest `agents-rel-*` tag with release-relevant content. There is no
detection ("missing release" alert) and no belt (an independent periodic
main-vs-tag comparison that re-dispatches the release). The failure is silent
by construction.

**Impact**: Any silently dropped push event = agents-side fixes dead in main
until a human notices. The tick engine rides the latest release tag, not main,
so a missing release freezes the whole machine loop (#826 hung).

**Fix approach**: Add the belt the ticket's capability surface prescribes — an
**agent-pack-release kicker**, independent of the SM tick engine (which itself
rides the release tag — it cannot be the only safety net for a broken release
path):

- `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release-kicker.yml` — scheduled every 10 min +
  `workflow_dispatch`; compares main HEAD vs the latest `agents-rel-*` tag,
  diffs since the tag, and dispatches `agent-pack-release.yml` when main is
  ahead on non-ignored paths and no release run is pending. Idempotent: the
  release workflow's own ledger/no-release guard dedupes (AC2), and an
  in-flight release run suppresses the dispatch.

#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * Agent pack release builder (dmtools-agents#441).
 *
 * Computes the affected agent set from the git diff since the last release,
 * bumps each affected agent's version in versions.json, builds EVERY agent
 * pack with `dmtools compile` (the single implementation of the pack format —
 * dm.ai#595), validates each zip against its manifest, and writes a FULL
 * catalog.json (every agent -> its current version): each release is a
 * self-contained snapshot because the registry resolver resolves
 * `<agent>@latest` against the newest release's catalog only.
 *
 * Usage:
 *   node ci/release_packs.mjs [--agents=all|name1,name2] [--bump=patch|minor|major]
 *       [--base-ref <git-ref>] [--prev-release-tag <tag>] [--allow-unverified-base]
 *       [--out dist] [--dry-run]
 *
 * Exit 0 with an empty affected set means "nothing to release" (not an error).
 *
 * gh-812 release integrity (live incident 2026-10-09): the builder derives
 * every version from the PREVIOUS RELEASE's shipped catalog (append-only,
 * cannot be rewritten by a failed ledger push) rather than versions.json on
 * main (--prev-release-tag; a failed shipped-state read FAILS the release
 * unless --allow-unverified-base opts into the ledger fallback), re-version
 * an unbumped agent whose
 * rebuilt payload differs from what its unchanged version already shipped
 * (never republish changed content under a shipped version), and gate every
 * built zip through the require sanity check (assertZipRequires) BEFORE the
 * ledger commit and the publish — a pack whose code requires a file the zip
 * does not carry must fail the release, not the fa runners.
 */

} from 'node:fs';

{"content":"# Agent pack release kicker (dmtools-agents#844).
#
# Belt for the silently-dropped push trigger (live 2026-10-10: #841 merged
# 14:24Z, no release until an operator dispatch 17:05Z — #826 hung in the
# gap). Every tick compares origin/main HEAD against the newest agents-rel-*
# tag and re-dispatches agent-pack-release.yml when main is ahead on
# non-ignored paths and no release run is pending. The push trigger stays —
# belt AND suspenders; the release workflow's own ledger guard + no-release
# no-op keep a double dispatch from cutting a duplicate release (gh-690).
name: Agent Pack Release Kicker

on:
  schedule:
    # gh-844 AC1: no agents-side fix may wait >15 min in main without a
    # release cut — a 10-minute cadence detects within one tick.
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write # gh workflow run agent-pack-release.yml
  contents: read # compare main against the latest release tag

concurrency:
  # Ticks must queue, never overlap: two concurrent ticks could both observe
  # no pending run and double-dispatch.
  group: agent-pack-release-kicker
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  kick:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history + tags for the since-tag diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Fetch main + release tags
        # The named-ref fetch alone only updates FETCH_HEAD; write the
        # remote-tracking ref and the tags explicitly so the diff below
        # always sees current main and every agents-rel-* tag.
        run: |
          git fetch origin \
            '+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main' \
            'refs/tags/*:refs/tags/*'

      - name: Kick agent-pack-release when main is ahead
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: node ci/release_kicker.mjs

# gh-844: [GOAL] Agent-pack release not cut on main merges after 11:25 — fixes sit dead in main (live: #841 sweep 2.75h to live; #826 hung)

## Description

## Goal

Agents-side machine fixes become live ONLY when a new agent-pack release is cut (the tick engine rides the latest release tag, not main). The release must be cut on EVERY agents-relevant main merge, reliably — today the push trigger silently skipped two consecutive merges (gh-840 sweep sat in main 2.75h before an operator dispatch; #826 hung the whole time).

## Subject

`.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml` push trigger reliability. Timeline 2026-10-10: releases at 07:11 / 07:29 / 08:47 / 09:33 / 09:38 / 09:52 / 11:25 — then SILENCE. Main pushes at 14:24 (#841, files: js/common/reworkConsumption.js, js/smAgent.js, js/unit-tests/*, sm_github.json — all outside paths-ignore .github|docs|site) and ~16:0x (#843) triggered NOTHING. Workflow state=active, file unchanged since 2026-10-09. Operator workflow_dispatch 17:05 cut agents-rel-... manually.

## Capability surface

- Detection: a main merge touching non-ignored paths with NO release run within N minutes → the release is MISSING; alert/dispatch.
- Belt: the SM tick (or a kicker rule) compares latest release tag's commit vs main HEAD each tick; when main is ahead on non-ignored paths and no release run is pending → dispatch workflow_dispatch (idempotent, safe — the workflow computes the affected set itself).
- Optional: reconcile the webhook-loss theory (check GitHub delivery logs) — if push events for machine merges are being dropped, the belt above is the durable fix regardless.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: no agents-side fix waits >15 min in main without a release cut (metric on the board or tick log line).
2. AC2: manual dispatch remains safe/idempotent (no double release for the same content — the version ledger dedupes).
3. AC3: docs/README paths still don't cut releases (paths-ignore preserved).
4. AC4: live — after ship, #841-class fixes activate without operator involvement.

## Test plan

- L1: rule unit tests (main-ahead detection with ignored-path diffs).
- L2: replay the 2026-10-10 14:24-17:05 timeline — the belt would have fired at ~14:39.
- L3 (live): next agents fix merges; release appears without human action.

## Non-goals

- Changing the pack format or compile steps.
- The release workflow's internal steps — only its TRIGGERING reliability.

## References

- Instance: #841 merged 14:24Z; no release until operator dispatch 17:05Z; #826 hung in the gap.
- Context: fa engine pin incident 2026-10-10 (factory_ref) — same "fix merged ≠ live" class.

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

This is a GOAL ticket about reliability of `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml` push trigger. The ticket asks for a "belt" — the SM tick (or a kicker rule) compares latest release tag's commit vs main HEAD each tick; when main is ahead on non-ignored paths and no release run is pending → dispatch workflow_dispatch.

Wait — this is a bug development pack. The ticket is gh-844. Let me look at the repo structure to understand what exists. The instructions say write RCA, write a reproduction test that fails, then fix.

The task: The push trigger silently skipped merges. The durable fix: a kicker in the SM tick that detects main-ahead-on-non-ignored-paths and dispatches workflow_dispatch.

Let me explore the repo: .github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml, js/smAgent.js, js/common/, js/unit-tests/.

# Agent pack release (dmtools-agents#441).
#
# Builds and publishes per-agent versioned packs — one self-contained zip per
# affected agent (<agent>-<version>.zip + manifest.json + .sha256) — so
# consumers fetch a single agent over plain HTTPS instead of a git submodule.
#
# The pack format is built by `dmtools compile` (dm.ai#595) — the runtime repo
# owns the single implementation; this workflow only orchestrates: test →
# compute affected set → bump versions.json → compile → validate → publish.
#
# Triggers:
#   push to main            — affected set from the diff since the last release tag
#   workflow_dispatch       — manual; `agents=all` or `agents=name1,name2`,
#                             `bump` selects patch/minor/major (default patch)
name: Agent Pack Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      # CI-only changes never cut a release. NOTE: '**.md' is deliberately
      # NOT ignored — agent instruction packs ship .md files (instructions/
      # joined the default agents in a57b3ba); ignoring them let runner
      # configs reference pack files the published zips never carried
      # (live: 2026-10-01 dev-leg failure, story_development-0.1.11).
      - '.github/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'site/**'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agents:
        description: "'all' or a comma-separated agent list (default: affected set)"
        required: false
        default: ''
      bump:
        description: 'Version bump'
        required: false
        default: 'patch'
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
      dry_run:
        description: 'Build + validate without publishing'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: agent-pack-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # publish the GitHub Release + commit versions.json

jobs:
  release:
    # The JS unit-test suite is NOT re-run here (owner 2026-10-01): quality.yml
    # runs it on every PR and main's protection is strict (required `crap` +
    # up-to-date), so every commit reaching main already passed the suite on a
    # current head. The release only computes the affected set, compiles,
    # validates and publishes.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history for the since-last-release diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' resolves to the current release tag (owner mandate 2026-10-01).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
            TAG="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "DMTOOLS_VERSION=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "::notice::dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${TAG}"
          fi

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        env:
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION || vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Compute base ref (last release tag, if any)
        id: base
        run: |
          last_tag=$(git tag --list 'agents-rel-*' --sort=-creatordate | head -1)
          echo "ref=${last_tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "base ref: ${last_tag:-<none — first release, all agents>}"

      - name: Sync to current main (queued runs release current main)
        # The concurrency group serializes release runs, but actions/checkout
        # gives each run its own TRIGGER SHA — a run queued behind another
        # computed its affected set and version bumps from a ledger that
        # pre-dated the previous run's ledger PR (live 2026-10-04, gh-690:
        # three content PRs merged within 3 min → overlapping releases
        # double-bumped sm_github/pr_review to 0.1.24 and cut the empty
        # ledger PR #689). Reset to origin/main so base-tag...HEAD covers
        # exactly the unreleased content ONCE, from the current ledger; a
        # queued run that finds everything already released writes
        # dist/.no-release and no-ops. Gated to push events — a manual
        # dispatch may deliberately target a non-main ref.
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        run: |
          git fetch origin main
          git reset --hard origin/main

      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
          # gh-812: the builder reads the previous release's shipped catalog
          # and same-version pack zips (version uniqueness + payload compare).
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # gh-812 rework (review thread 3): untrusted tag names reach the
          # script ONLY through env indirection — never template-expanded
          # into the run: block. Actions interpolates ${{ }} BEFORE bash
          # parses the script, so a crafted agents-rel-* tag name (any user
          # with push access can create one; the newest by creatordate wins)
          # could break out of the quoting and run arbitrary code in this
          # contents:write job.
          BASE_REF: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
          PREV_RELEASE_TAG: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-812 rework: release-base tags are machine-generated
          # (agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS); anything else in the newest
          # agents-rel-* tag is rejected before it reaches the builder.
          # Empty is allowed — the first release has no base tag.
          for tag in "${BASE_REF}" "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}"; do
            if [ -n "${tag}" ] && ! [[ "${tag}" =~ ^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$ ]]; then
              echo "::error::unexpected agents-rel tag format: ${tag}" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          args=(--out dist)
          [ -n "${AGENTS}" ] && args+=(--agents="${AGENTS}")
          [ -n "${BASE_REF}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${BASE_REF}")
          # gh-812: base versions come from what the last release SHIPPED —
          # versions.json on main is a best-effort ledger that can (and did)
          # lag reality by whole releases, re-shipping a live version with
          # new content.
          [ -n "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}" ] && args+=(--prev-release-tag="${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}")
          [ "${DRY}" = "true" ] && args+=(--dry-run)
          [ "${BUMP}" != "patch" ] && args+=(--bump="${BUMP}")
          node ci/release_packs.mjs "${args[@]}"
          # Signal "nothing to release" to the publish steps.
          if [ -f dist/.no-release ]; then echo "released=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "released=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

      - name: "Bump versions.json via PR (protection-clean)"
        # Rulesets on personal repos have no bypass actors and no PAT scope
        # can edit them from CI (HTTP 404, live 2026-10-01) — a direct push
        # to main can NEVER satisfy required checks. So the bump rides a
        # side branch + PR + squash merge: quality.yml's crap check
        # satisfies the ruleset. The squash subject carries [skip ci] so the
        # merge push does not re-trigger a release (paths-ignore does not
        # cover versions.json).
        #
        # Nothing-changed guard (gh-690): a server-side auto-merge fires the
        # moment the checks pass and cannot re-verify that main did not move
        # while the PR waited — #689 merged with a 0-byte diff because its
        # branch was cut before the previous ledger PR landed. Instead: skip
        # creating the PR when main already carries the target versions
        # (gu…

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml.
# This repo's validation CI is `Quality` (display name "Quality") and its
# required context is the `crap` job.
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  # dmtools-agents#682 (live fa#1202/#1203 2026-10-03, still reproducing
  # 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22 in THIS repo — runs 06:36/06:41/06:43): the
  # global group below already ran with cancel-in-progress:false, yet
  # kicker runs kept dying cancelled in chains. cancel-in-progress only
  # shields the RUNNING run — a queued run in the same group ALWAYS
  # supersedes (cancels) the pending one (GitHub docs: "Any existing
  # pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists,
  # will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its
  # place"). One global group meant every push anywhere (silent refresh,
  # factory-data snapshots, dev waves) cancelled every other branch's
  # pending kicker. Per-head-SHA group: no push can displace another
  # push's kicker — a queued kicker that is about to dispatch a tick
  # always gets to run (canonical fix + consumer notes: IstiN/
  # dmtools-agentic-workflows factory-sm-kicker.yml). Effective once the
  # canonical pin is bumped (separate PR): until then the called
  # workflow's own global group still supersedes.
  group: sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  kicker:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: quality.yml
      ci_display_name: Quality
      required_contexts: crap

# Quality gate — CRAP ratchet via crap4js, pinned like crap4dart in dmd.
#
# Threshold policy (owner 2026-09-28): the CRAP bar is NOT lowered to pass —
# the CURRENT measured maximum is fixed as the ratchet baseline, so the code
# can only improve. Baseline: 4879.8 (action/developTicketAndCreatePR.js,
# CC=116 @ 29.3% coverage). Improvements lower the max freely; any change
# that pushes the max ABOVE the baseline fails the gate.
#
# Tool pin: crap4js v0.8.1 by release tag (same discipline as dmd pinning
# crap4dart 0.9.5). Install from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js' package is an
# unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Ratchet baseline — the measured repo-wide maximum CRAP (see header).
  # Re-measure with the steps below; lower it when the code improves.
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '4879.8'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'v0.8.1'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: crap4js gate (ratchet — baseline ${{ env.CRAP_THRESHOLD }})
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}"

Good. Now let me design the fix following the repo patterns:

**Root cause**: GitHub push events for machine merges were dropped (webhook-loss theory, unconfirmed) — push trigger of `agent-pack-release.yml` silently skipped two main merges. No detection/belt exists.

**Fix**: Add a release kicker — durable belt:
1. New workflow `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release-kicker.yml` — schedule every ~10 min + workflow_dispatch, permissions `actions: write, contents: read`; runs a small step that uses `gh` to:
   - fetch main HEAD SHA and latest `agents-rel-*` tag commit
   - if tag commit == main HEAD → noop
   - diff tag...main names-only; filter through the paths-ignore list (`.github/**`, `docs/**`, `site/**`); if nothing relevant → noop
   - check runs of agent-pack-release.yml queued/in_progress → if any, noop
   - else `gh workflow run agent-pack-release.yml --ref main`
2. New guard module `ci/release_kicker_guard.cjs` with pure testable logic mirroring the workflow:
   - `IGNORED_PATTERNS` / `isIgnoredPath(path)`
   - `filterRelevantFiles(files)`
   - `decideReleaseKick({mainHead, lastReleaseCommit, changedFiles, activeRuns})` → 'dispatch'|'noop' with reason.
3. Tests: new `js/unit-tests/test_releaseKicker.js` + `run_releaseKicker.json`, added to run_all.json:
   - L1: path classification (AC3: .github/docs/site ignored; js/, sm_github.json, README.md, versions.json relevant)
   - L2: replay 2026-10-10 14:24 timeline: main ahead, files js/common/reworkConsumption.js, js/smAgent.js, js/unit-tests/x, sm_github.json, no active runs → decision dispatch
   - idempotency: active run pending → noop (AC2)
   - HEAD == tag commit → noop
   - only ignored files changed → noop
   - workflow wiring: kicker workflow exists, schedule present, paths-ignore list matches the release workflow's paths-ignore exactly (single source of truth concern — the workflow has its own embedded bash; test asserts both contain same patterns), dispatch uses gh workflow run.

The kicker workflow's bash: to avoid duplicating the ignore list in two places... the release workflow's paths-ignore is YAML in agent-pack-release.yml. The kicker can't easily read that at runtime. Options: kicker step greps paths-ignore from the workflow file in checkout. That's actually elegant and keeps a single source of truth:

```bash
mapfile -t IGNORED <(awk '/paths-ignore:/,/^  workflow_dispatch:/' .github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml | sed -n 's/^ *- *'\''\([^'\'']*\)'\''.*/\1/p')
```

Hmm, fragile. Simpler: the pure logic in `ci/release_kicker_guard.cjs` exports `pathsIgnoreFromWorkflowYml(yml)`? But the kicker runs in GitHub Actions with node available — the kicker step can be a node one-liner that requires the guard. Actually following the established split ("pure CommonJS twin keeps decisions unit-testable"), I'll write the kicker as a small node script `ci/release_kicker.mjs` that imports `ci/release_kicker_guard.cjs` (pack_release_guard precedent: ESM imports CJS). {"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# gh-844 — Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The agent-pack release (`agent-pack-release.yml` push trigger) silently
skipped two consecutive main merges on 2026-10-10 (14:24Z gh-841, ~16:00Z gh-843);
agents-side fixes sat unreleased in main for 2.75h until an operator's manual
`workflow_dispatch` (17:05Z), hanging #826 in the gap.

**Root cause**: The release pipeline has exactly ONE trigger plane — the GitHub
`push` event on main. When a push event is dropped server-side (webhook-loss
theory; delivery logs not reconciled), nothing anywhere detects that main is
ahead of the latest `agents-rel-*` tag with release-relevant content. There is no
detection ("missing release" alert) and no belt (an independent periodic
main-vs-tag comparison that re-dispatches the release). The failure is silent
by construction.

**Impact**: Any silently dropped push event = agents-side fixes dead in main
until a human notices. The tick engine rides the latest release tag, not main,
so a missing release freezes the whole machine loop (#826 hung).

**Fix approach**: Add the belt the ticket's capability surface prescribes — an
**agent-pack-release kicker**, independent of the SM tick engine (which itself
rides the release tag — it cannot be the only safety net for a broken release
path):

- `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release-kicker.yml` — scheduled every 10 min +
  `workflow_dispatch`; compares main HEAD vs the latest `agents-rel-*` tag,
  diffs since the tag, and dispatches `agent-pack-release.yml` when main is
  ahead on non-ignored paths and no release run is pending. Idempotent: the
  release workflow's own ledger/no-release guard dedupes (AC2), and an
  in-flight release run suppresses the dispatch.
- `ci/release_kicker_guard.cjs` — pure, unit-testable decision logic (same
  CJS-guard + ESM-runner split as `pack_release_guard.cjs`/`release_packs.mjs`),
  parsing the `paths-ignore` list **from the release workflow itself** so the
  ignore set has a single source of truth (AC3).
- `ci/release_kicker.mjs` — thin gh/git runner executing the guard's decision.

**Previous attempt**: none (fresh ticket, not returned).
"}

#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * Agent pack release builder (dmtools-agents#441).
 *
 * Computes the affected agent set from the git diff since the last release,
 * bumps each affected agent's version in versions.json, builds EVERY agent
 * pack with `dmtools compile` (the single implementation of the pack format —
 * dm.ai#595), validates each zip against its manifest, and writes a FULL
 * catalog.json (every agent -> its current version): each release is a
 * self-contained snapshot because the registry resolver resolves
 * `<agent>@latest` against the newest release's catalog only.
 *
 * Usage:
 *   node ci/release_packs.mjs [--agents=all|name1,name2] [--bump=patch|minor|major]
 *       [--base-ref <git-ref>] [--prev-release-tag <tag>] [--allow-unverified-base]
 *       [--out dist] [--dry-run]
 *
 * Exit 0 with an empty affected set means "nothing to release" (not an error).
 *
 * gh-812 release integrity (live incident 2026-10-09): the builder derives
 * every version from the PREVIOUS RELEASE's shipped catalog (append-only,
 * cannot be rewritten by a failed ledger push) rather than versions.json on
 * main (--prev-release-tag; a failed shipped-state read FAILS the release
 * unless --allow-unverified-base opts into the ledger fallback), re-version
 * an unbumped agent whose
 * rebuilt payload differs from what its unchanged version already shipped
 * (never republish changed content under a shipped version), and gate every
 * built zip through the require sanity check (assertZipRequires) BEFORE the
 * ledger commit and the publish — a pack whose code requires a file the zip
 * does not carry must fail the release, not the fa runners.
 */

} from 'node:fs';

{"content":"# Agent pack release kicker (dmtools-agents#844).
#
# Belt for the silently-dropped push trigger (live 2026-10-10: #841 merged
# 14:24Z, no release until an operator dispatch 17:05Z — #826 hung in the
# gap). Every tick compares origin/main HEAD against the newest agents-rel-*
# tag and re-dispatches agent-pack-release.yml when main is ahead on
# non-ignored paths and no release run is pending. The push trigger stays —
# belt AND suspenders; the release workflow's own ledger guard + no-release
# no-op keep a double dispatch from cutting a duplicate release (gh-690).
name: Agent Pack Release Kicker

on:
  schedule:
    # gh-844 AC1: no agents-side fix may wait >15 min in main without a
    # release cut — a 10-minute cadence detects within one tick.
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write # gh workflow run agent-pack-release.yml
  contents: read # compare main against the latest release tag

concurrency:
  # Ticks must queue, never overlap: two concurrent ticks could both observe
  # no pending run and double-dispatch.
  group: agent-pack-release-kicker
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  kick:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history + tags for the since-tag diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Fetch main + release tags
        # The named-ref fetch alone only updates FETCH_HEAD; write the
        # remote-tracking ref and the tags explicitly so the diff below
        # always sees current main and every agents-rel-* tag.
        run: |
          git fetch origin \
            '+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main' \
            'refs/tags/*:refs/tags/*'

      - name: Kick agent-pack-release when main is ahead
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: node ci/release_kicker.mjs
","path":".github/workflows/agent-pack-release-kicker.yml"}

# gh-844: [GOAL] Agent-pack release not cut on main merges after 11:25 — fixes sit dead in main (live: #841 sweep 2.75h to live; #826 hung)

## Description

## Goal

Agents-side machine fixes become live ONLY when a new agent-pack release is cut (the tick engine rides the latest release tag, not main). The release must be cut on EVERY agents-relevant main merge, reliably — today the push trigger silently skipped two consecutive merges (gh-840 sweep sat in main 2.75h before an operator dispatch; #826 hung the whole time).

## Subject

`.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml` push trigger reliability. Timeline 2026-10-10: releases at 07:11 / 07:29 / 08:47 / 09:33 / 09:38 / 09:52 / 11:25 — then SILENCE. Main pushes at 14:24 (#841, files: js/common/reworkConsumption.js, js/smAgent.js, js/unit-tests/*, sm_github.json — all outside paths-ignore .github|docs|site) and ~16:0x (#843) triggered NOTHING. Workflow state=active, file unchanged since 2026-10-09. Operator workflow_dispatch 17:05 cut agents-rel-... manually.

## Capability surface

- Detection: a main merge touching non-ignored paths with NO release run within N minutes → the release is MISSING; alert/dispatch.
- Belt: the SM tick (or a kicker rule) compares latest release tag's commit vs main HEAD each tick; when main is ahead on non-ignored paths and no release run is pending → dispatch workflow_dispatch (idempotent, safe — the workflow computes the affected set itself).
- Optional: reconcile the webhook-loss theory (check GitHub delivery logs) — if push events for machine merges are being dropped, the belt above is the durable fix regardless.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: no agents-side fix waits >15 min in main without a release cut (metric on the board or tick log line).
2. AC2: manual dispatch remains safe/idempotent (no double release for the same content — the version ledger dedupes).
3. AC3: docs/README paths still don't cut releases (paths-ignore preserved).
4. AC4: live — after ship, #841-class fixes activate without operator involvement.

## Test plan

- L1: rule unit tests (main-ahead detection with ignored-path diffs).
- L2: replay the 2026-10-10 14:24-17:05 timeline — the belt would have fired at ~14:39.
- L3 (live): next agents fix merges; release appears without human action.

## Non-goals

- Changing the pack format or compile steps.
- The release workflow's internal steps — only its TRIGGERING reliability.

## References

- Instance: #841 merged 14:24Z; no release until operator dispatch 17:05Z; #826 hung in the gap.
- Context: fa engine pin incident 2026-10-10 (factory_ref) — same "fix merged ≠ live" class.

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

This is a GOAL ticket about reliability of `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml` push trigger. The ticket asks for a "belt" — the SM tick (or a kicker rule) compares latest release tag's commit vs main HEAD each tick; when main is ahead on non-ignored paths and no release run is pending → dispatch workflow_dispatch.

Wait — this is a bug development pack. The ticket is gh-844. Let me look at the repo structure to understand what exists. The instructions say write RCA, write a reproduction test that fails, then fix.

The task: The push trigger silently skipped merges. The durable fix: a kicker in the SM tick that detects main-ahead-on-non-ignored-paths and dispatches workflow_dispatch.

Let me explore the repo: .github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml, js/smAgent.js, js/common/, js/unit-tests/.

# Agent pack release (dmtools-agents#441).
#
# Builds and publishes per-agent versioned packs — one self-contained zip per
# affected agent (<agent>-<version>.zip + manifest.json + .sha256) — so
# consumers fetch a single agent over plain HTTPS instead of a git submodule.
#
# The pack format is built by `dmtools compile` (dm.ai#595) — the runtime repo
# owns the single implementation; this workflow only orchestrates: test →
# compute affected set → bump versions.json → compile → validate → publish.
#
# Triggers:
#   push to main            — affected set from the diff since the last release tag
#   workflow_dispatch       — manual; `agents=all` or `agents=name1,name2`,
#                             `bump` selects patch/minor/major (default patch)
name: Agent Pack Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      # CI-only changes never cut a release. NOTE: '**.md' is deliberately
      # NOT ignored — agent instruction packs ship .md files (instructions/
      # joined the default agents in a57b3ba); ignoring them let runner
      # configs reference pack files the published zips never carried
      # (live: 2026-10-01 dev-leg failure, story_development-0.1.11).
      - '.github/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'site/**'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agents:
        description: "'all' or a comma-separated agent list (default: affected set)"
        required: false
        default: ''
      bump:
        description: 'Version bump'
        required: false
        default: 'patch'
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
      dry_run:
        description: 'Build + validate without publishing'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: agent-pack-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # publish the GitHub Release + commit versions.json

jobs:
  release:
    # The JS unit-test suite is NOT re-run here (owner 2026-10-01): quality.yml
    # runs it on every PR and main's protection is strict (required `crap` +
    # up-to-date), so every commit reaching main already passed the suite on a
    # current head. The release only computes the affected set, compiles,
    # validates and publishes.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history for the since-last-release diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' resolves to the current release tag (owner mandate 2026-10-01).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
            TAG="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "DMTOOLS_VERSION=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "::notice::dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${TAG}"
          fi

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        env:
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION || vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Compute base ref (last release tag, if any)
        id: base
        run: |
          last_tag=$(git tag --list 'agents-rel-*' --sort=-creatordate | head -1)
          echo "ref=${last_tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "base ref: ${last_tag:-<none — first release, all agents>}"

      - name: Sync to current main (queued runs release current main)
        # The concurrency group serializes release runs, but actions/checkout
        # gives each run its own TRIGGER SHA — a run queued behind another
        # computed its affected set and version bumps from a ledger that
        # pre-dated the previous run's ledger PR (live 2026-10-04, gh-690:
        # three content PRs merged within 3 min → overlapping releases
        # double-bumped sm_github/pr_review to 0.1.24 and cut the empty
        # ledger PR #689). Reset to origin/main so base-tag...HEAD covers
        # exactly the unreleased content ONCE, from the current ledger; a
        # queued run that finds everything already released writes
        # dist/.no-release and no-ops. Gated to push events — a manual
        # dispatch may deliberately target a non-main ref.
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        run: |
          git fetch origin main
          git reset --hard origin/main

      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
          # gh-812: the builder reads the previous release's shipped catalog
          # and same-version pack zips (version uniqueness + payload compare).
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # gh-812 rework (review thread 3): untrusted tag names reach the
          # script ONLY through env indirection — never template-expanded
          # into the run: block. Actions interpolates ${{ }} BEFORE bash
          # parses the script, so a crafted agents-rel-* tag name (any user
          # with push access can create one; the newest by creatordate wins)
          # could break out of the quoting and run arbitrary code in this
          # contents:write job.
          BASE_REF: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
          PREV_RELEASE_TAG: ${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-812 rework: release-base tags are machine-generated
          # (agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS); anything else in the newest
          # agents-rel-* tag is rejected before it reaches the builder.
          # Empty is allowed — the first release has no base tag.
          for tag in "${BASE_REF}" "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}"; do
            if [ -n "${tag}" ] && ! [[ "${tag}" =~ ^agents-rel-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}$ ]]; then
              echo "::error::unexpected agents-rel tag format: ${tag}" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          args=(--out dist)
          [ -n "${AGENTS}" ] && args+=(--agents="${AGENTS}")
          [ -n "${BASE_REF}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${BASE_REF}")
          # gh-812: base versions come from what the last release SHIPPED —
          # versions.json on main is a best-effort ledger that can (and did)
          # lag reality by whole releases, re-shipping a live version with
          # new content.
          [ -n "${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}" ] && args+=(--prev-release-tag="${PREV_RELEASE_TAG}")
          [ "${DRY}" = "true" ] && args+=(--dry-run)
          [ "${BUMP}" != "patch" ] && args+=(--bump="${BUMP}")
          node ci/release_packs.mjs "${args[@]}"
          # Signal "nothing to release" to the publish steps.
          if [ -f dist/.no-release ]; then echo "released=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "released=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

      - name: "Bump versions.json via PR (protection-clean)"
        # Rulesets on personal repos have no bypass actors and no PAT scope
        # can edit them from CI (HTTP 404, live 2026-10-01) — a direct push
        # to main can NEVER satisfy required checks. So the bump rides a
        # side branch + PR + squash merge: quality.yml's crap check
        # satisfies the ruleset. The squash subject carries [skip ci] so the
        # merge push does not re-trigger a release (paths-ignore does not
        # cover versions.json).
        #
        # Nothing-changed guard (gh-690): a server-side auto-merge fires the
        # moment the checks pass and cannot re-verify that main did not move
        # while the PR waited — #689 merged with a 0-byte diff because its
        # branch was cut before the previous ledger PR landed. Instead: skip
        # creating the PR when main already carries the target versions
        # (gu…

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml.
# This repo's validation CI is `Quality` (display name "Quality") and its
# required context is the `crap` job.
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  # dmtools-agents#682 (live fa#1202/#1203 2026-10-03, still reproducing
  # 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22 in THIS repo — runs 06:36/06:41/06:43): the
  # global group below already ran with cancel-in-progress:false, yet
  # kicker runs kept dying cancelled in chains. cancel-in-progress only
  # shields the RUNNING run — a queued run in the same group ALWAYS
  # supersedes (cancels) the pending one (GitHub docs: "Any existing
  # pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists,
  # will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its
  # place"). One global group meant every push anywhere (silent refresh,
  # factory-data snapshots, dev waves) cancelled every other branch's
  # pending kicker. Per-head-SHA group: no push can displace another
  # push's kicker — a queued kicker that is about to dispatch a tick
  # always gets to run (canonical fix + consumer notes: IstiN/
  # dmtools-agentic-workflows factory-sm-kicker.yml). Effective once the
  # canonical pin is bumped (separate PR): until then the called
  # workflow's own global group still supersedes.
  group: sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  kicker:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: quality.yml
      ci_display_name: Quality
      required_contexts: crap

- Detection: a main merge touching non-ignored paths with NO release run within N minutes → MISSING release; alert/dispatch.

Where would this belt live?
